Ribeirão Preto offers a side of Brazil rarely included in a typical beach itinerary. Travel here revolves around agribusiness, exhibitions and business meetings. The city lies inland in São Paulo state, in a region known for sugarcane cultivation and the production of sugar and ethanol. This is where Agrishow, a major agricultural machinery exhibition, takes place.

After the professional program, it is worth making time for the historic center. The Pedro II Theater, which opened in 1930, forms part of the Quarteirão Paulista architectural ensemble. Its facade, the square and the surrounding buildings are an invitation to walk around the city and discover its cultural life. Concerts and performances can be selected according to the current schedule.

Ribeirão Preto suits travelers who want to combine a trip to Brazil with their professional interests. You can come here from São Paulo for a separate business stop and then continue your journey to the Amazon, Rio de Janeiro or Iguaçu Falls. The specific event, dates and company visits are agreed upon for the chosen trip.

During major exhibitions, it is best to arrange accommodation and transport in advance. A date in a tour's name does not, by itself, confirm that a particular conference will take place. The schedule of business events should be checked before booking.

## Volcanoes, Mud Springs and Rafting: What to See in Rincón de la Vieja, Costa Rica

Rincón de la Vieja National Park covers more than 14 hectares and is considered part of the Guanacaste province's protected natural area in northwestern Costa Rica. The park takes its name from the volcano at its center.

Rincón de la Vieja is an active complex volcano consisting of nine active and extinct craters. Its most recent eruptions occurred in 2017 (May 23 and June 11), while its largest eruption took place around 3,500 years ago. Despite its activity, Rincón de la Vieja is not considered dangerous and is open to tourists.

## Activities in Rincón de la Vieja National Park

Rincón de la Vieja National Park is a popular tourist destination where you can observe nature, see traces of volcanic activity, bathe in mud springs and go rafting on the river. Visitors can enjoy walks through the park, horseback rides, rafting, off-road vehicle excursions and rock climbing.

Río Celeste attracts visitors with the unusual blue color of its water. The river runs through humid forest in the Tenorio National Park area. A local legend explains its hue this way: after creating the sky, God washed his paintbrushes in the river. The story accompanies an introduction to a natural phenomenon that is especially visible at Los Teñideros.

Walking trails lead to stretches of the river and the Río Celeste waterfall. The color of the water contrasts with the green surrounding forest and the pale stones of the riverbed. Both the river itself and the forest vegetation around it are worth exploring. This is a place to discover the natural environment of northern Costa Rica on foot.

## Canoeing Along Forested Riverbanks

On the Rio Claro River, travelers discover the southern edge of the Amazon rainforest from the water. The canoe route offered by Jardim da Amazônia Lodge heads toward Anaconda Lake, offering views of riverside vegetation and opportunities for birdwatching.

Anna's Word document mentions kingfishers, herons, cormorants and tanagers. Which birds you encounter depends on which species are near the river during your outing. The river excursion complements the walking trails around the lodge.

This is the river near Jardim da Amazônia Lodge in the São José do Rio Claro area, not one of the waterways with the same name near Chapada dos Guimarães.

Rio da Prata is located in the natural area around Bonito and Jardim in Mato Grosso do Sul state. Its clear freshwater lets visitors see fish, the sandy riverbed and dense underwater vegetation. This underwater landscape is the area's defining feature.

Exploring the river combines a walk through the natural surroundings with snorkeling downstream. Routes also include the Olho d'Água spring area. Rio da Prata complements land-based outings around Bonito with a chance to see life in a freshwater river.
